cross_case_findings: Across these single runs, all arms completed cases 01, 02, 03, and 05; the main divergences were recovery from read-only Git metadata in case 04 and bytecode side effects in case 06.
Contract A and Contract B were complementary on direct evidence, preservation, root-cause investigation, and fresh verification, but those areas were also the principal source of redundant coverage.

Static conflict recurred where Contract B’s mandatory questions, approval, specification, plan, commits, tests, or branch-finishing choices contradicted exact task instructions. Correct task-instruction precedence was not treated as failure.

No arm asked an unnecessary question or made an unnecessary commit. The material avoidable writes were two speculative source candidates in case-01 Lambda, substitute-repository configuration in case-04 Kappa, and cache creation/cleanup in case-06 Lambda or retained cache in case-06 Mu.

Case-04 Kappa achieved the exact remote commit/ref and matching temporary-local/remote OIDs, but not the requested local branch in the original workspace; the other two arms preserved exact scope but remained blocked by read-only Git metadata.
Case-06 demonstrates that a correct diagnosis and clean final prose do not by themselves establish full task success when trace or fixture evidence shows prohibited file mutation.

All metrics used the same “Codex CLI turn.completed usage” semantics. Timing and token records were inspected descriptively, but no causal or general performance conclusion is drawn from one run per arm.

All metadata reported exit status 0 and all cleanup records reported authentication and temporary-root removal; those transport/cleanup facts were not treated as proof of task success or verification.
